`recall --evidence` returns `<system-reminder>…</system-reminder>` text as `role: "user"` evidence when it is the content of a user turn. This happens with native claude-code records, both when `message.content` is a plain string and when it is a text block:

```json

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"<system-reminder>…</system-reminder>"}]}}
```

`docs/recall-evidence.md` (lines 42-43) says: "Structured hidden reasoning, tool output, system instructions and metadata are not returned as conversation text." That holds for system-role records, which the evidence path drops. It doesn't hold for reminder text inside a user turn.

The other conversation readers already skip these turns. In the run below, `conversationSubstantiveRequest` returns "" for both reminder lines, while the evidence path returns them as user spans. In that run the two reminder spans also came out ahead of the real user request.

### Repro

`main` @ f8deab17, Go 1.27.3, linux/amd64, run in a clean `env -i` with a throwaway HOME/GOPATH/GOCACHE. This is a throwaway test in `internal/cli` (not committed). {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"<system-reminder>zebrafoo block-form reminder</system-reminder>"}]}}
```
{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"please fix the zebrafoo parser"}]}}
{"type":"assistant","message":{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Fixed the zebrafoo parser."}]}}
{"type":"system","content":"zebrafoo system-role record"}
```

Output:

```
state=available warnings=[] spans=4
EVIDENCE line=1 pointer=/message/content role="user" text="<system-reminder>zebrafoo string-form reminder</system-reminder>"
EVIDENCE line=2 pointer=/message/content/0/text role="user" text="<system-reminder>zebrafoo block-form reminder</system-reminder>"
EVIDENCE line=4 pointer=/message/content/0/text role="assistant" text="Fixed the zebrafoo parser."

CONVERSATION line=1 conversationSubstantiveRequest=""
CONVERSATION line=2 conversationSubstantiveRequest=""
CONVERSATION line=3 conversationSubstantiveRequest="please fix the zebrafoo parser"
```

The system-role record on line 5 is dropped as expected. Lines 1 and 2 are returned as user evidence.

Compact v1 transcripts don't produce evidence on `main` at all yet. #564 adds that, and with #564 compact `<system-reminder>` user turns behave the same way. I didn't change that in #564 because this gap predates compact support.

Wrapper or system-reminder text inside a user turn isn't returned as user conversation evidence, the same way system-role records aren't.

The evidence path uses neither.

### Possible direction (your call)

One option is to skip user-role fields in `evidenceJSONFields` when the text matches the same wrapper predicate the other readers use. Another is a narrower check just for `<system-reminder>`-style wrappers. Note that `isWrapperRequest` drops any user text that starts with `<`, which may be broader than you want for evidence. The third option is to keep the behavior and change the docs to say that reminder text inside a user turn can show up. Which one fits the evidence contract is up to you.

Related to #412 and #534, and a companion to #560. **This PR is based on `main` and doesn't depend on #560.** It builds, passes and can merge either before or after #560 (details under "Relation to #560"). Not marked as fixing either issue, for the same reason as #560: #557 fixed the main symptom, and I don't know whether you consider those issues done.

The commits don't carry `Entire-Checkpoint` trailers. I don't have a supported agent session to capture them from, and I didn't want to fake any.

## Why

Compact v1 records (`{"v":1,"type":"user"|"assistant","content":[...]}`, what the default export writes for claude-code, codex and pi) put the content at the record's top level, with no `message` wrapper. #557 taught the conversation, history-fragment and eval-gen readers to read that. Three more readers still look only inside `message`, and each one is broken on `main` (failing output below):

- **`episode_tools.go`**: `toolCallsFromObj` reads assistant content only from `message.content`. In a compact session it finds no `tool_use` blocks, so every episode has empty `ToolSequence` / `CommandSequence`. Episode segmentation on `main` already recognizes compact user turns, so the episodes exist but have no tools in them.
- **`pattern_corpus_enrich.go`**: `corpusEpisodeOps` has the same problem, so compact sessions add no `episode_tools`, `episode_commands` or file refs to the pattern corpus.
- **`recall_evidence_source.go`**: `evidenceJSONFields` produces no fields for compact records. Every compact session is marked `partial` with "contains unreadable or unsupported conversation content" and never returns an evidence span. Compact user text blocks also have no `type` (`{"text":"..."}`), and compact records keep the turn time in `ts`, not `timestamp`.

## What changed

- `episode_tools.go`, `pattern_corpus_enrich.go`: when a record has no `message` wrapper, read the assistant content from the top level. This is the same fallback `history.go` and `conversation.go` already use on `main`.
- `recall_evidence_source.go`: if a `user`/`assistant`/`message` record has no `message` key, its content is read from the top level with JSON pointers under `/content`, untyped `{"text":...}` blocks are accepted, and `ts` is used when `timestamp` is absent. All three only apply to records without a `message` key, so native claude-code, codex and opencode parsing is unchanged. Tool output (`tool_use.result`), images and thinking blocks are still excluded.
- `patterns.IndexerVersion` 9 → 10. The corpus skips a session when its size, mtime, sha and parser version are unchanged. A compact transcript's bytes don't change on upgrade, so without the bump, sessions already indexed with empty tool ops would stay that way. Earlier reader changes bumped this version the same way (see `docs/pattern_v2.md`).
- Episode projection versioned too. The bump above only reaches the SQLite corpus. `refreshPatternLayer` skips rebuilding `patterns/episodes.ndjson` (and the tasks, procedures and practices built from it) while the sessions fingerprint is unchanged, and an upgrade doesn't change it. The patterns source in the manifest now records `extraction_version` (the `patterns.IndexerVersion` that built the episodes), and `patternSourceCurrent` treats a different version as stale. Sources written before the field read as 0 and rebuild once. `patterns status` uses the same check, so it reports them `stale` until then.

Two commits: the reader fix with the version bump, then the episode-projection version and compact `ts`.

**Rebased onto current `main` (6c4b11de).** The only conflict was in `episodes.go`. #589 removed `PrivacyIdentity` from the pattern source. So `patternSourceCurrent` now compares only the sessions fingerprint and `ExtractionVersion`, and the `ExtractionVersion` it writes is just `patterns.IndexerVersion`. The commit message was updated to match.

## Relation to #560

#560 adds a `transcriptRecordContent` helper and compact fixtures in `history_compact_transcript_test.go`. This PR uses neither, so it doesn't depend on #560:

- The two tool-op readers use `main`'s existing inline fallback instead of the helper. If #560 merges, they can switch to `transcriptRecordContent` in a one-line follow-up.
- The fixtures live in `compact_transcript_ops_fixtures_test.go`, under different names (`compactOps{Claude,Codex,Pi}Transcript`), so the two PRs don't declare the same symbols. Their content is the same as #560's fixtures. Once both are in, one set can be deleted.
- Both PRs add an `ExtractionVersion` field to `internal/manifest`, but on different structs (`PatternSource` here, `HistorySource` in #560).

Checked against #560 rebased onto the same `main` (b7b4fb55): merging it with this branch is clean (git merge, no conflicts), and on the merged tree `go test ./internal/cli/... -count=1` passes. So it doesn't matter which one merges first.

## Tests

- `TestEpisodeToolSequencesCompactTranscript`, `TestBuildBrainEpisodesCompactTranscriptToolSequences` (the second goes through `buildBrainEpisodes`)
- `TestCorpusEpisodeOpsCompactTranscript`, `TestPatternCorpusReindexesCompactTranscriptToolOps`. The second builds the corpus, then models a v9 corpus (parser_version 9, tool ops deleted) and rebuilds.
- `TestRecallEvidenceCompactTranscript`: checks the exact fields per line, role and pointer. It also checks that every pointer resolves to the reported string in the source line, that no tool output leaks, and that each field's timestamp is the record's `ts`.
- `TestRefreshPatternLayerRebuildsEpisodesFromOlderExtractor`: builds the episode layer, rewrites it the way the old reader left it (same episodes, no tool ops, no `extraction_version`), then runs a normal (non-forced) `refreshPatternLayer`.

Here is the overview of PR #564.

**The problem it fixes**

Compact v1 transcripts are the format the default export writes for claude-code, codex, and pi sessions. A compact record looks like `{"v":1,"type":"user","content":[...]}` — the content sits at the top level, with no `message` wrapper. PR #557 taught the main conversation and history readers to handle that shape, but three readers still looked only inside `message`. On `main`, each one silently failed on compact sessions:

1. **Episode tools** (`episode_tools.go`): episodes from compact sessions had empty tool and command sequences.
2. **Pattern corpus** (`pattern_corpus_enrich.go`): compact sessions added no tool ops or file refs to the pattern corpus.
3. **Recall evidence** (`recall_evidence_source.go`): every compact session was marked `partial` ("unreadable or unsupported") and returned no evidence spans.

**The fix**

- The two tool-op readers fall back to the record's top-level `content` when there is no `message` key. This copies the fallback `history.go` and `conversation.go` already use.
- The evidence reader does the same, and also accepts two compact quirks: text blocks with no `type` field, and the timestamp living in `ts` instead of `timestamp`. All of it applies only to records without a `message` key, so the native formats parse exactly as before.

**The cache-invalidation part** (the subtle half of the PR)

Fixing the readers is not enough. Both the pattern corpus and the episode layer skip rebuilds when the session files look unchanged — and a compact transcript's bytes do not change when the binary upgrades. So sessions already indexed with empty tool ops would stay wrong forever. The PR handles that twice:

- `patterns.IndexerVersion` bumps 9 → 10, which invalidates the SQLite corpus.
- The manifest's `PatternSource` gains an `extraction_version` field, and `patternSourceCurrent` treats a different version as stale. That forces one rebuild of `episodes.ndjson` and everything derived from it. Manifests written before the field read as version 0, so they rebuild once too.

**Tests**

Six new test functions cover all three readers, including a rebuild test that models an old v9 corpus and a stale episode layer. Each failure mode is pinned: the tests fail on unpatched `main`.

**What I changed to make it ready**

The PR predated #603, so one test still expected the compact fixture's `<system-reminder>` turn as user evidence. I merged current `main` in and removed that line — the planned one-line follow-up. Full suite, gofmt, and vet pass on the merged tree.

# transcript

Package `github.com/entireio/cli/transcript` converts native agent transcripts
into the Entire Transcript Format and reads that format into typed Go values.

The library is versioned with CLI releases. Its API and the format may change;
consumers should pin a version.

## Entire Transcript Format v1

The format has been called the "compact transcript" (CLI code, metadata key
`compact_transcript`) and the "unified transcript" (entire-api). All three names
refer to the same thing. Stored names are unchanged: the file is
`transcript.jsonl`, the metadata key is `compact_transcript`, and the line field
is `cli_version`.

One JSON object per line, each line terminated by `\n`.

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v` | int | yes | Always `1`. |
| `type` | string | yes | `user` or `assistant`. |
| `agent` | string | no | The CLI agent registry name (`claude-code`, `codex`, `copilot-cli`, `cursor`, `factoryai-droid`, `opencode`, `pi`, `antigravity`); otherwise the agent type string, e.g. for external agents. An open set. |
| `cli_version` | string | no | Version of the producer that wrote the line. The name is historical. |
| `ts` | string | no | Source timestamp where available, normally RFC 3339. May be omitted or empty when the native transcript has no timestamp. The generic JSONL converter copies source timestamps verbatim, so a non-string value can occur; readers ignore it. |
| `id` | string | no | Assistant message ID. Streaming fragments with the same ID are merged into one line. The Codex item path writes the item ID on user lines too. |
| `model` | string | no | Assistant lines only. The model the source reports for this call, verbatim; omitted when it reports none. Never inferred from a session-wide default, and never a placeholder: a value the agent writes in place of a model (Claude Code's `<synthetic>` on API-error entries) is omitted. |
| `input_tokens` | int | no | Assistant lines only. Input not counted in the line's `cache_read_tokens` or `cache_write_tokens`; see below. |
| `output_tokens` | int | no | Assistant lines only; includes reasoning tokens when the source reports them as part of output. |
| `cache_read_tokens`, `cache_write_tokens` | int | no | Assistant lines only; per-call cached input read and total cached input written. Cache counts are separate from fresh `input_tokens`. |
| `cache_write_5m_tokens`, `cache_write_1h_tokens` | int | no | Assistant lines only; an optional breakdown of `cache_write_tokens`, emitted only when the source reports the split (even when a reported value is zero). Absence means unknown, not zero or all 5m. Do not add the split to the total when summing usage. |
| `reasoning_tokens` | int | no | Assistant lines only; subset of `output_tokens` when reported by the source, not additional output. |
| `content` | array of blocks, string, or `null` | yes | Normally an array. A string can appear when an assistant message's source content was a string. `null` can appear because the writer does not omit empty content. |

Usage and model fields are per call, never copied from a session aggregate. A zero omitted by JSON encoding does not assert that the source reported zero.

On every line, `input_tokens` excludes the tokens in that line's `cache_read_tokens` and `cache_write_tokens`, so adding them never double counts. The sum is the call's total input only on lines from a converter that writes the cache fields. Lines written before that carry no cache fields, and their `input_tokens` is one of two things:

- Fresh input only (Claude Code, and Pi except as below): the cached input is missing from the line, so the sum understates the call's input.
- Fresh plus cached input (Codex, and Pi on Google models before pi-ai subtracted cached tokens in March 2026): the total is right, but its cache share is unknown, so pricing it at the fresh-input rate overstates the cost.

Other agents' lines copy the native input count as the agent defines it. Only `agent` and the `cli_version` that wrote a line tell these cases apart; no field marks a line as old or new, and `model` in particular says nothing about how `input_tokens` was counted.

Converters fill only what the native transcript reports per call. Claude Code, Codex and Pi record per-call usage and model, and their converters write them (below). Copilot CLI has only a shutdown aggregate, Cursor is hook-only, and external plugins and Antigravity report usage out of band, so their lines do not get these fields. Native timestamps are preserved where present; a missing one stays empty rather than fabricated.

### Per-call usage

An assistant line can carry usage with empty content (`"content":[]` or `"content":null`, for example an aborted or thinking-only call): readers that render transcripts should skip it, and readers that count usage must keep it.

Fresh input is `input - cached` clamped at zero; Codex lines carry no cache-write fields. A user message ends the open call. With `StartLine`, the skipped lines seed the usage baseline, and the last line before the boundary is part of the slice when its call's closing snapshot arrives after it (a one-line head overlap).

Abandoned branches are excluded. Read per-call usage from the full converted transcript. - User text: `{"id"?: string, "text": string}`. There is no `type` field (a v1 quirk).
- Assistant text: `{"type": "text", "text": string}`.
- Tool use: `{"type": "tool_use", "id"?: string, "name": string, "input": any, "result"?: {"output": string, "status": "success"|"error", "file"?: {"filePath": string, "numLines"?: int}, "matchCount"?: int, "agent"?: {"id": string}}}`.

You're right that a canonical parser exists — but it lives in `entireio/cli`, not entiredb. The `entiredb` repo (entirehq org) is the storage service; it has no transcript parser.

**What exists: `github.com/entireio/cli/transcript`**
- Its README says it "converts native agent transcripts into the Entire Transcript Format and reads that format into typed Go values."
- It documents every quirk PR #564 just re-implemented by hand: user text blocks with no `type` field, the `ts` timestamp field, `null`/empty content, and `tool_use` blocks with inlined results.
- It is written for external consumers: "The library is versioned with CLI releases… consumers should pin a version." The API docs even note entire-api reads the same format.

**Why entire-brain doesn't use it today**
- entire-brain's `go.mod` has zero entireio dependencies. Nothing in Brain records a decision against importing it — recall returns no such memory. The closest recorded principle actually supports you: "the brain must reuse platform infrastructure rather than introduce its own."

**Where it would fit, and where it would not**
- The two tool-op readers (`episode_tools.go`, `pattern_corpus_enrich.go`) only need typed content blocks. They could use the library directly. Same for the conversation and history readers.
- The evidence reader is the hard one. Evidence spans address byte ranges in the original field string, and `content_sha256` binds that exact string, with a JSON pointer per field. A typed-value parser throws that positional information away. That reader would keep its own JSON walking, or the library would need a lower-level API.

**My recommendation**
- Merge #564 as-is. It is small, tested, and ready now.
- File a follow-up to adopt `entireio/cli/transcript` in the readers where typed values suffice, pinned to a CLI release. That removes the class of "one more reader missed the compact shape" bugs — this PR is the third such fix after #557 and #560.

Three PRs have now fixed the same class of bug: a reader that only understood the native \`message\`-wrapped record shape and silently failed on compact (ETF v1) transcripts — #557 (conversation, history-fragment, eval-gen readers), #560 (history compact readers), #564 (episode tools, pattern corpus, recall evidence). Each fix re-implements the same format knowledge by hand: top-level \`content\`, user text blocks with no \`type\` field, \`ts\` instead of \`timestamp\`, \`null\`/empty content.

A canonical parser already exists: \`github.com/entireio/cli/transcript\`. Its README documents every one of these quirks, reads ETF v1 into typed Go values, and is written for external consumers (\"versioned with CLI releases; consumers should pin a version\"). entire-api already reads the same format.

## Scope

Adopt the library in the readers where typed content blocks are sufficient:

- \`episode_tools.go\` (\`toolCallsFromObj\`)
- \`pattern_corpus_enrich.go\` (\`corpusEpisodeOps\`)
- the conversation / history readers where they duplicate ETF shape handling

Pin a CLI release in go.mod. This is entire-brain's first entireio dependency, so keep the import surface to the \`transcript\` package.

## Out of scope

\`recall_evidence_source.go\` keeps its own JSON walking. Evidence spans address byte ranges in the original field string, \`content_sha256\` binds that exact string, and each field carries a JSON pointer into the source line. A typed-value parser discards that positional information. Revisit only if the library grows a lower-level API that preserves source positions.

## Risks

- The library's API and the format can change between CLI releases; the pin must be bumped deliberately.
- Behavior differences between the library's reading and the current hand-rolled readers (for example thinking-block handling) need test coverage before the switch: the existing compact-transcript tests from #557/#560/#564 should pass unchanged." 2>&1 | tail -1

Fixes #566, fixes #567

## Why

This fixes compact codex `apply_patch` file refs. I asked on #566 to be assigned and haven't heard back yet. If someone else is already on this, I'm happy to close it.

**This depends on #564.** It's stacked on #564's current head (`ebf7c6c8`, which is on `main` `6c4b11de`). Until #564 merges, this PR's diff also shows #564's two commits. The rest are new: `24b55dbe` for #566, the two commits from #602 (`bb1a698b`, `02d16560`) and `1afc32da` for #567, plus two merges of `main`. I'll rebase onto `main` once #564 lands. It can't stand alone on `main`: compact records never reach `claudeContentOps` there, and the compact fixtures come from #564. Against current `main` (`fb99b029`) the branch merges cleanly (`git merge-tree`) and the full suite passes on the merge (see Tests).

A compact v1 codex `apply_patch` `tool_use` has no path field. For older Codex rollouts the cli converter (its `response_item` path) wraps the `custom_tool_call` patch text as `{"input": <patch>}` (`codexCustomToolUseBlock`, entireio/cli `transcript/codex.go`). `claudeContentOps` only looked at `file_path` / `path` / `filename`, so the block gave no file refs. The same patch from a native `custom_tool_call` gives one ref per `*** Add/Update/Delete File` line. That left a patch-only compact turn with no write ref, so `classifyEpisodeShape` labelled it `read_only`, which also made it eligible for themes.

## What changed

- `internal/cli/pattern_corpus_enrich.go`: if `apply_patch` has no path, `claudeContentOps` now runs `patchFiles` on `input.input`, the same helper the native `custom_tool_call` case uses. An explicit path still takes priority. (+5 lines)
- `internal/cli/patterns/runs.go`: `IndexerVersion` 10 → 11 (#564 takes it 9 → 10). The corpus skips a session when its size, mtime, sha and parser version are all unchanged, and a compact transcript's bytes don't change on upgrade, so without the bump sessions indexed by the version 10 reader would keep their missing file refs and `read_only` shapes.

### Versions and #575

I kept this in line with #575's approach (wire/schema versions stay readable by stable clients; only an extractor revision moves):

- Only `patterns.IndexerVersion` changes. Through #564 the same constant is the patterns source's `extraction_version` in the manifest, so the episode projection rebuilds once; `corpusEpisodeOps` is only called by the corpus indexer, so `episodes.ndjson` comes out the same.
- No schema version changes, and the history scan cache is not touched (`historyScanCacheVersion` / `historyScanCacheWireVersion` from #575 stay as they are): `claudeContentOps` is only reached from `corpusEpisodeOps`, which the history scan doesn't use.
- One thing for #564 rather than this PR: `extraction_version` is a new field in the manifest, and a pre-#564 build's manifest writer decodes strictly, so after a #564+ build refreshes a brain, an older build sharing it refuses to rewrite the manifest (run on `main` `fb99b029`: tolerant read drops the field; strict write path returns "brain manifest carries a field this build does not know (json: unknown field "extraction_version")"). This PR only changes the value, not whether the field is there.

## Ordering with the #567 fix

This PR also carries the #567 fix (below), folded in from #602 as evisdren suggested on #567, so `patterns.IndexerVersion` is bumped once (10 → 11).

## Tests

- `TestCorpusEpisodeOpsCompactTranscript`: the codex row #564 pinned as `files: nil` now expects `edit internal/cli/export.go`.
- `TestCorpusEpisodeOpsCompactApplyPatchMatchesNative` (new): one patch with Add, Update and Delete. Native and compact must give the same refs (`add docs/new.md,edit internal/cli/export.go,delete old.go`), and `apply_patch` with an explicit `path` still gives just that path.
- `TestPatternCorpusCompactApplyPatchShapesWrite` (new): goes through `buildPatternCorpus` with #564's codex fixture. The episode shapes must be `0:shell,1:write` and `episode_files` must have the edit. It then models a version 10 corpus (`parser_version=10`, file refs deleted), rebuilds, and checks that both are back.

  - Revision 13 covers the null/empty `message` fallback below. Earlier builds of this branch wrote revision 12 without that fallback, and their caches would otherwise stay current.   - `docs/memory-storage-compatibility.md` now says revision 13.
- **Short-term overlay: format stays 3 and gains `extractor_version`.** An earlier version of this PR bumped `historyShortTermVersion` 3 → 4 instead. A build without the change also couldn't read a v4 overlay. I confirmed both by running them. Now the overlay keeps format 3 and records the extraction revision. A delta carries an unchanged file's entry forward only when the overlay's `extractor_version` matches the current revision. So an old overlay with an empty entry for a compact transcript is still readable, and that file is re-parsed on the next delta. Such an overlay has the v3 layout without `extractor_version`, so it's now read as v3 with an unknown extractor: it stays in retrieval, isn't counted as complete, and the next delta rewrites it as v3. Before this, the overlay loaded as unsupported and doctor said to upgrade. `TestHistoryShortTermReadsLegacyV4Overlay` uses a real overlay written by one of those builds. Version 4 is reserved now, so the "unknown newer overlay" health test uses 5.

The warning, and the overlay's partial-coverage text, give the revision and say whether it's older or newer than this binary's. Before, data from a newer binary was also called "older". Behaviour is unchanged: any other revision is re-parsed, as with the scan cache.

## Why

Since entireio/cli#2897 (shipped in cli 0.13.1), the cli converts a current Codex rollout through its items. Two things it writes weren't read:

- A failed command is a compact `Bash` block with `result.status:"error"`. Its output is the command's own, with no exit text, and the rollout's `exit_code` isn't carried over. The corpus stored it as `exit_code=NULL, failed=0`, so it was missing from `exit_fails`.
- An edit is a `FileChange` block with `input.changes[].path` (absolute) and `kind`. It gave no file ref, so a turn whose only edit was a `FileChange` had no write ref.

## The two defaults

1. **A `Bash` block with status `"error"` is stored as failed, with `exit_code` NULL.** It counts in `exit_fails`. This is only for compact codex `Bash` blocks; claude-code and pi `status:"error"` are still not read (that's #567's open question). The cli writes `"error"` when an item failed **or was declined** ([`codexitem.Item.Failed`](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/3a760b96a60fe1bf68f70bc1c164257df7b43e9e/internal/transcript/codexitem/item.go#L84-L91), used at [`codex_items.go#L78`](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/3a760b96a60fe1bf68f70bc1c164257df7b43e9e/transcript/codex_items.go#L75-L80)), so a command the user declined counts as failed too. The compact record can't tell them apart. If that's wrong, the other way is for the cli to carry the exit code (or the declined status) in the compact result.
2. **A `FileChange` path is stored relative to the repo root of the session that wrote it.** The session's checkpoint already records the files it touched relative to the repo (`files_touched`), so a candidate root is what's left of a `FileChange` path once a touched file is stripped from its end: `/home/ada/src/repo/cmd/main.go` with `cmd/main.go` touched gives `/home/ada/src/repo`. A candidate scores one for each distinct session path that is a touched file under it, and the highest score wins, so a checkout named like one of its own directories or repeated edits of one file can't pick the wrong root. Every path under the winner is stored relative to it, so the ref links to symbols the way an `apply_patch` path does. A path outside the root is kept as written, as a Claude `file_path` is today. So is every path of a session whose touched files match none of them or whose top score is tied, since a wrong root would link edits to the wrong files, and so is any path with a `..` segment, since the OS resolves `..` after symlinks. A session with such a path gets no root at all, since leaving it out could hand the root to the rest. The other way is for the cli to write repo-relative paths (it knows the rollout's `cwd`).

The second default goes further than my comment on #600 said. Because the root comes from the session rather than from the checkout building the corpus, a session from a sibling worktree or a teammate's machine is made relative too, and the stored refs are the same whichever checkout runs `refresh`.

`kind` maps `add`, `delete` and `update` to `add`, `delete` and `edit`; any other kind is an `edit`. An `update` with a `move_path` is a `delete` of the old path plus an `add` of the new one. Like an `apply_patch`, a change counts whatever its result status.

Both accept `/` and `\` separators. Scores are counted in one pass over each path's `/` splits, so a long session stays linear.
- `pattern_corpus.go`: `indexSessionIntoCorpus` infers the root once per session and passes it to `corpusEpisodeOps`. Since the root comes from the checkpoint's `files_touched`, `corpusSessionUnchanged` also compares the checkpoint a session was exported from (the `checkpoint_id` already in `indexed_sessions`), so a later checkpoint of the same transcript re-indexes it.

Then a corpus reset to indexer version 11 is re-indexed on the next build.

If you'd rather pin another one, it's a one-line `go.mod` change. Pre-review on the fork, with the review bots' threads: Beehtrix/entire-brain#25.

## Why

#557, #560 and #564 each fixed the same bug in a different reader: it knew only the native `"message"`-wrapped record and read nothing from a compact transcript (Entire Transcript Format v1). Each fix re-implemented the format by hand. The CLI already parses that format into typed values in `github.com/entireio/cli/transcript`, so brain now uses it. Your four hardening notes from the #601 review are folded in, as you asked on the issue.

## Commits

1. **`78d87f4` build: require Go 1.27.3 and `github.com/entireio/cli` v0.13.1.** It's brain's first entireio module. `transcript` imports only the standard library, so no new third-party packages come with it. The cli module says `go 1.27.3`, so brain's `go 1.27` + `toolchain go1.27.2` becomes `go 1.27.3`, and `mise.toml`, the CI `go-version` pins, CONTRIBUTING, README and the getting-started and reference docs move with it. Minimum version selection also moves `go-git/v6` to the pseudo-version cli uses (`v6.0.0-beta.1.0.20261105090440-f07160f87eaa`) and bumps a few indirect modules (x/crypto, x/net, x/sync, x/text, go-winio, colorprofile, xo/terminfo). `scripts/install.sh` compared only major and minor Go versions, so a Go 1.27.2 with `GOTOOLCHAIN=local` passed its check and then failed to build. It now compares the patch version too.
2. **`56f4432` refactor: read compact transcripts with the cli transcript package.** Every reader decodes a line once with `decodeTranscriptRecord` (new `transcript_record.go`). A line with an integer `v` and a non-empty string `type` (the test `transcript.Parse` uses) goes through `transcript.Decode`, and the readers work on its typed `Line` and `Block` values. Any other line keeps the native readers (Claude Code's `"message"` wrapper, Codex rollout records, pi's `"message"` records), which brain still needs for raw `full.jsonl` transcripts. Readers moved: episode tool calls, the pattern corpus ops, the conversation narrative, request and tool-name readers, history fragments, distill's conversation text, and the user text eval-gen and reinforcement read. `recall_evidence_source.go` is left as it is, as the issue says.
3. **`ae9e727` fix(patterns): key compact codex exit text on the call's input shape** (notes 1, 2 and 4; the skip rule is revised in commit 7). The shared tool-call reader normalizes the tool name once, so every check sees the same one. The compact `apply_patch` fallback also reads a bare string `input` as the patch.
4. **`62cf266` fix(patterns): read exit codes only from Codex's wrapper header** (note 3). When an `Output:` line is present, only the header before it is searched, so exit-like text the command printed (a test logging `child process exited with code 1`, or a running command that reports `Process running with session ID N`) can't stand in for the wrapper's exit line. Text with no such line is read as before. Native `function_call_output` records and compact results share the parser, so both change.
5. **`c6d6987` docs(changelog)**: an Unreleased Fixed entry for commit 4.
6. **`79208f4` fix(transcript): keep what the old readers read from rejected and wrapped lines.** A user or assistant line the package rejects (another `v`, or a known field of the wrong JSON type) is read from its top-level content, as every reader did on main. History's native `tool_use` branch mines an inlined `result.output` again.
7. **`a53bdc8` fix(patterns): skip item-path command output by the Bash name, not the input shape.** On note 4: the input shape isn't the item path's alone. Codex's own `shell_command` tool also takes a `"command"` string (OpenAI's Codex prompting guide types it as a string), and its output is the wrapper text with the exit code. So the skip keys on the normalized name `bash`, which the item path gives every command and Codex's own tools never use. It still ignores case and spacing, and covers a JSON-encoded input. An explicit exit code in the compact result would let the corpus drop the check; that would be a cli change.

- Reader output is unchanged for every line the CLI writes, so the history extraction revision stays at 13.
- The precedence `transcriptRecordContent` pinned is kept in the decoder: a non-empty `"message"` wrapper wins, and a user or assistant record with a null, empty or missing `"message"` has its top-level content read.
- Distill now reads the top-level content of a user or assistant record whose `"message"` is null or `{}`, as the other readers already did (cab0496).
